plan_title: MONITORING, REPORTING, AND VERIFICATION PLAN Bull Moose AGI #1 Targa Delaware, LLC (Targa)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA; the regulatory AMA (end-of-injection plume in 2055 plus half a mile, and the 2060 plume) lies inside it (p47-49).
mma_definition: The stabilized plume at 2070 (1% saturation cutoff) plus a half-mile buffer; nearby faults lie outside, so no fault buffer was added (p48-49).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment, especially the well and its pipeline, is called a potential risk though very unlikely; drilling new wells through the injection zone could cause a surface release; three offset wells get a medium risk rating. Confining zone, lateral migration, faults and seismicity are very unlikely (p51-61).
baseline_summary: Planned 12 months of monthly groundwater sampling and soil CO2 flux measurements before moving to less frequent sampling, a seismic baseline from historical TexNet data, and H2S levels seen during inspections; DCS flags excursions in operating parameters (p67-70).
reporting_summary: Annual GHG reports and supporting records retained (period not stated). Targa says it will report data from its monitoring network and produce periodic seismic and groundwater chemistry reports, but names no recipient and makes no commitment to publish; TexNet data are public (p66, p68-69, p76).

rows.detail: Volumetric flow meter and sampling point on the TAG line before the well, with daily totalizers on receiving and injection meters; CO2 concentration by consensus standard methods.
rows.location: TAG line upstream of BM AGI #1 (FM and SP in Figure 3.7-1)
rows.evidence_quote: Daily CO2 injected is recorded by totalizers on the volumetric flow meters on the pipelines to the BM AGI #1 well

rows.detail: Plant DCS continuously monitors injection rate, pressure and composition with high/low set points; qualified technicians follow response protocols when alerts fire.
rows.location: BM AGI #1 and plant surface equipment
rows.trigger_or_response: Parameter outside allowable window: engineering and operations alerted, investigation; confirmed leak: shut in well, quantify, remediate.
rows.evidence_quote: The DCS of the plant monitors injection rates, pressures, and composition on a continuous basis.

rows.detail: MITs of BM AGI #1 under TRRC Class II testing rules; interval not stated.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT indicating leak: shut in well, quantify leak from operating conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: requirements for testing and monitoring of Class II injection wells to ensure they maintain mechanical integrity at all times

rows.detail: In-well pressure/temperature gauges to be installed so bottomhole injection pressure stays below 90% of fracture gradient; gauge depth and reading interval not given.
rows.trigger_or_response: Readings outside acceptable range: well shut in and leak characterized and quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitoring systems will be installed to ensure that bottomhole injection pressure does not exceed 90% of the determined fracture gradient of the injection interval.

rows.detail: Field personnel follow daily and weekly inspection protocols for surface equipment; routine operations and maintenance procedures include frequent periodic inspection of the well.
rows.location: Plant surface equipment and BM AGI #1
rows.trigger_or_response: Detected leak reported and responded to; surface-equipment leaks isolated and quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: following daily and weekly inspection protocols which include reporting and responding to any detected leakage events.

rows.detail: Personnel and contractors in sour areas wear H2S monitors alarming at 10 ppm; handheld O2/LEL/H2S/CO2 detectors used to check areas before maintenance work.
rows.location: Worn by plant personnel; handheld units at strategic plant locations
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: response under the H2S Contingency Plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Personal monitoring devices will give an audible alarm and vibrate at 10 ppm.

rows.detail: Numerous fixed H2S monitors across the plant tied to PLCs and the DCS (alarm 10 ppm, evacuation 90 ppm); in-field monitors also detect CO2.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm triggers immediate response to address and characterize the situation; evacuation at 90 ppm H2S.
rows.evidence_quote: Targa also maintains in-field gas monitors to detect H2S and CO2.

rows.detail: Soil CO2 flux measured with a LI-COR LI-8100A chamber on fixed PVC collars: monthly for a 12-month baseline, bimonthly for a year, then quarterly.
rows.location: Pre-planned collar locations at the site (number not stated)
rows.trigger_or_response: Leaks traced to the subsurface are quantified using flux monitoring methods.
rows.evidence_quote: Soil CO2 flux will be collected on a monthly basis for 12 months to establish the baseline

rows.detail: Groundwater wells sampled monthly for 12 months, bimonthly for a year, then quarterly; TDS, pH, ions, ORP, IC, NPOC. Which wells is unclear.
rows.location: Groundwater wells in the MMA (not identified)
rows.trigger_or_response: Results outside expected variation: investigate whether leakage from the injection zone occurred.
rows.evidence_quote: Water samples will be collected and analyzed on a monthly basis for 12 months to establish baseline data.

rows.detail: Distributed temperature sensing to be deployed in BM AGI #1, alongside P/T gauges, to monitor leakage and wellbore integrity.
rows.evidence_quote: pressure and temperature gauges as well as Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS) will be deployed in Targa’s BM AGI #1 well.

rows.detail: Operator seismometer and recorder installed at the plant to meet TRRC requirements, plus TexNet network data analyzed by Targa with periodic event reports; historical data as baseline.
rows.location: Bull Moose plant station plus surrounding TexNet stations
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic event linked to surface leakage: assess whether CO2 came from BM AGI #1 and quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: Targa has Installed a seismometer and a digital recorder to monitor for and record data for any seismic event at the Bull Moose Gas Plant.

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic used to build the static model and pick faults for the fault slip analysis; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: The examination of faults identified from the 3D seismic data

rows.detail: Plan says other wells in the MMA will be watched by an 'atmospheric and CO2 flux monitoring network', but no atmospheric method, location or frequency is described.
rows.location: Vicinity of other wells in the MMA
rows.evidence_quote: Other wells within the MMA will be monitored with the atmospheric and CO2 flux monitoring network placed strategically in their vicinity.

rows.detail: Inline inspections listed as a detection method for surface equipment.
Track TRRC applications for permits to drill and inject, and alert operators active in the MMA that it has CO2/H2S injection.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitor applications for permit to drill and permit to inject made to the TRRC

rows.detail: When drilling into the injection zone: H2S monitored at many surface locations, slower drilling, closer mud-return monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitoring H2S at surface at many locations (H2S can be a proxy to detect CO2)

rows.detail: Reassess plume migration modeling if monitoring shows the plume beyond the modeled area.
rows.trigger_or_response: Plume beyond modeled area: reassess modeling and submit revised MRV plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Targa will reassess the plume migration modeling for evidence that the plume may have intersected a pathway for CO2 migration.

rows.detail: Subpart W Table W-1A emission factors for equipment between meter and wellhead; detected leaks quantified with mass flow meters, leak-rate models or operating conditions.
rows.location: Surface equipment between injection meter and wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: the emissions factor listed in Table W-1A of Subpart W shall be used to estimate all streams of gases.

notes: BM AGI #1 was permitted but not yet drilled (drilling planned Q4 2024), so in-well gauges and DTS are future commitments; the seismometer is described as already installed. Groundwater well count conflicts: p35 lists 2 domestic wells in the MMA, p55 says there are none, so sampling locations are unknown. Atmospheric monitoring is only named once (p67), so coded mentioned_only. No annulus monitoring is mentioned. Text cites a New Mexico rule (NMAC) for a Texas site (p51) and AGA Report #1 for orifice metering. Post-injection monitoring is 15 years (p5, p63).
